text: Nine phase-nodes delivered across 10 runs: 70 files, +8237/-551, $13.60, 13.7h wall clock, silentStallRate 0. Full suite, typecheck, and both eval commands (17/17 deterministic, 17/17 discriminating) green on campaign/factory-autonomy-20260914. main untouched; promotion to main is the owner's call by this campaign's own policy. WHAT IT DELIVERED. A heartbeat with two independent fields and two thresholds, and a supervisor that acts on it even against a live lock. A persisted contract load that touches no filesystem beyond its own contract.json, which is what makes a drifted run resumable at all. Parked separated from terminal, with runOutcome, escalating re-nag, one persisted auto_retry, and dependants that wait instead of cascading. The chain: an ordered manifest, a landBranch that is never main without an explicit flag, idempotent promotion, and a coordinator that is an idempotent re-invocation rather than a daemon that cannot watch itself. A managed block that shows a parked run instead of erasing it, plus an append-only inbox. A loop that cannot be frozen by a child that never closes or by unbounded synchronous git. Seal before kill. And a judge prompt that no longer carries the output of tests that passed. PROVED ON ITSELF, THREE TIMES. Phase 5b landed seal-before-kill at 09:50; at 12:20 phase 6 stalled at 900s and its worktree was sealed (sealedSha da3be514, sealError null) -- before 5b that stall would have discarded the attempt, which is exactly how a recorded take lost 58 minutes mid-file. Phase 4's new warning is what surfaced that the Ford notification transport was never configured in this environment. And the composed tier pool walked GLM (quota_exhausted, 52 min) to Gemini (provider_error, 14 min) to DeepSeek inside a single node, with no operator: the never-stop rule working for real. IMPROVEMENT 1 -- the phase order is wrong for a campaign that runs on its own factory. Phase 6 contains the fix for the 64 KiB judge-prompt guard, and that guard killed the chain-plumbing node of this very campaign…
